[34mInvestigated:[0m Reviewed JSONStorage.__init__ and write in tinydb/storages.py, where stored kwargs are passed to json.dumps on each write. Checked existing sort_keys usages in tests/test_storages.py and docs/usage.rst, and the changelog format in docs/changelog.rst. Confirmed the working tree was clean before the edits.

[33mLearned:[0m The earlier plain sort_keys=True default crashes with TypeError on dicts that mix int and str keys, because json.dumps cannot order them. Catching that TypeError and retrying with keys ordered by str(key) lets those writes succeed. Existing db.json files will be rewritten in sorted order on their next write, producing one large diff on first commit. The test suite must run with -c /dev/null because pytest.ini requires the pytest-cov plugin, which is not installed.

[32mCompleted:[0m JSONStorage now defaults to sort_keys=True via setdefault, and sort_keys=False restores insertion order. A try/except around json.dumps falls back to a recursive _sort_keys_as_str helper for mixed-type keys. The JSONStorage docstring documents the default. Three tests were added to tests/test_storages.py covering the sorted default, the opt-out, and mixed int/str keys. An Unreleased entry was added to docs/changelog.rst. The full suite passes with 231 tests. git status shows three modified files: docs/changelog.rst, tests/test_storages.py, and tinydb/storages.py. Nothing has been committed.

[35mNext Steps:[0m No further steps were observed in this session. The change is in the working tree, awaiting review and a commit.

[36mNotes:[0m Expect one large fixture diff the first time db.json files are rewritten. The mixed-key fallback sorts by string form, so int keys sort lexically (for example "200" before "500"). Reading back still returns int keys as strings, which is existing behavior and not changed by this work.
